title: fix(app-shell): drop four flow-node defaultValue declarations the installed spec backs none of
body:
Fixes #9109

Executes triage's ruling on that card (its answered `pm:retriage` comment, id `5659536024`): **direction B — delete the declarations the installed spec backs none of.** This PR does not re-open that choice. The mechanical half (widening the reconciliation ledger past the approval-escalation block) landed earlier as objectui#9279.

`FlowConfigField.defaultValue` is documented in its own doc comment as **the spec default for this key**, and is acted on as one at three sites: `controllerAdmits` resolving an unset `showWhen` controller, the `boolean` control's checked seed (objectui#8451), and the `select` control's trigger placeholder (objectui#6830 arm A). A declaration with no spec counterpart is therefore **false by that definition**, and deleting it restores an invariant.

## The declaration table, re-derived from the INSTALLED Zod at the branch point

Branch point `72d6587`, installed `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0**. Read field by field off the Zod, not inherited from the card.

WARNING — the card's table has ten rows; the table on disk has **thirteen**. `approval.lockRecord` and `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.interrupting` (objectui#9277) and `end.outcome` (objectui#9278 / objectui#9337) all became declaring fields after the card was written. The dispatch's four line numbers were also not inherited; every row below is cited by content.

| declaring field | kind | declares | installed spec for an omitted key | action |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `approval.behavior` | select | `first_response` | applies `first_response` | keep |
| `approval.onEmptyApprovers` | select | `admin_rescue` | applies `admin_rescue` | keep |
| `approval.lockRecord` | boolean | `true` | applies `true` | keep |
| `approval.maxRevisions` | number | `3` | applies `3` | keep |
| `approval.escalation.enabled` | boolean | `true` | applies `true` | keep |
| `approval.escalation.action` | select | `notify` | applies `notify` | keep |
| `approval.escalation.notifySubmitter` | boolean | `true` | applies `true` | keep |
| `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.interrupting` | boolean | `true` | applies `true` | keep |
| `end.outcome` | select | `completed` | applies `completed` | keep |
| `http_request.config.method` | select | `GET` | optional, applies NOTHING | **deleted** |
| `screen.config.mode` | select | `create` | optional, applies NOTHING | **deleted** |
| `wait.waitEventConfig.eventType` | select | `timer` | **REQUIRED**, applies nothing | **deleted** |
| `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.eventType` | select | `error` | **REQUIRED**, applies nothing | **deleted** |

Nine remain, all of them backed. The four removed are exactly the four the card named.

## Delivery order: display vs submit, measured separately for each of the four

Triage required each deletion to be measured for whether it changes what the form **submits** or only what it **displays**. Measured on this tree in both states — declarations present, then deleted:

| deleted declaration | SUBMIT | DISPLAY |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `http_request.config.method` | unchanged | trigger placeholder `GET` becomes the "nothing is selected" mark. No gated siblings, so the visible field set is identical. |
| `screen.config.mode` | unchanged | trigger placeholder `Create` becomes the mark. No gated siblings. |
| `wait.waitEventConfig.eventType` | unchanged | trigger placeholder `Timer` becomes the mark, **and** `Duration` (gated on `timer`) is no longer revealed on a node storing no `eventType`. |
| `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.eventType` | unchanged | trigger placeholder `Error` becomes the mark, **and** `Error code` (gated on `error`) is no longer revealed on a node storing no `eventType`. |

**All four are display-only.** A declared default is shown, never written — objectui#6263's standing ruling keeps the write half out — so the submit channel cannot observe a declaration at all. Measured, not argued: rendering each affected node patches the draft **zero** times and leaves it unchanged **byte for byte**, in both tree states.

The sharpest evidence for that claim is in the ablation below: the four SUBMIT rows are the only new pins that stay **green** when the fix is removed. Their invariance across both legs is the measurement.

Config an author already stored is untouched. objectui#6499's stored-value re-show rule keeps a stored `timerDuration` / `errorCode` on screen regardless of its controller, and that is pinned beside each removal — without it, this change would be indistinguishable from one that hid an author's own data.

## The REQUIRED-key stop clause: NOT tripped

Triage's stop clause fires if deleting a declaration would leave a key the spec marks REQUIRED **with no value**. Two of the four are against REQUIRED enums, so this was expected to fire — it does not, and the measurement says why:

**a declared default was never a value on the key.** It is read at three sites and written at none, so `waitEventConfig.eventType` and `boundaryConfig.eventType` were unset before this change and are unset after it. An omitted key did not behave as `timer` / `error` at any point; it failed to parse. What the declaration supplied was not a value but an on-screen claim that leaving the key alone was a working configuration — in two ways at once, the revealed sibling and the stated placeholder.

So the clause's trigger condition never arises, and nothing here needs a spec default in order to keep working. Whether these keys *should* gain one is a separate product question — one decision card per field, filed when someone actually wants it — and deliberately **not** pre-booked here.

`packages/spec` and `node_modules/@objectstack/spec` were READ ONLY. The lane fence holds.

## Verification

Reverse verification, from the committed state. The fix was reverted with the branch point pinned by sha (never a moving remote-tracking name), the mutation was proved on disk by grep counts and a blob hash that differs from HEAD's, and restoration was proved by an empty `git diff HEAD` plus the blob hash returning to HEAD's.

- **fix absent:** `Test Files 2 failed (2)` · `Tests 17 failed | 62 passed | 1 skipped (80)`
- **fix present:** `Test Files 2 passed (2)` · `Tests 79 passed | 1 skipped (80)`

The 17 that redden name themselves: the four per-region "declares nothing the spec leaves unbacked" rows, the table-wide register equality, the four objectui#9109 spec-side rows, the four trigger rows, the two gated-sibling rows, the declaration-surface inventory and the select-kind sweep.

Other readings, all from real run output:

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — `Test Files 264 passed` · `Tests 2809 passed | 1 skipped`
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` — exit 0 (covers `src` and `tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test code is typechecked)
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the three changed source files — 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Narrowed from the repo-wide run deliberately: the file count is read from eslint's own `--format json` output, and type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js`, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide run remains CI's.
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:designer-field-key-parity` — all exit 0
- `check-changeset-presence` / `check-changeset-no-major` — exit 0; `Changeset Declaration` satisfied by a `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all four changed paths — NOT GOVERNED

## Notes for review

**The ledger's unbacked register is now empty, and its re-measurement was rewritten.** It used to be driven by `it.each` over the register's own rows, which contributes one case per row — so an emptied register would contribute **no** case, run nothing, and still report green. That is the exact vacuity shape the file already documents for its other register, so the walk now iterates the scope table instead: a region with no row answers with the positive statement, a region with a row re-measures the spec state that row claims. A new `DELETED_BY_9109` pin keeps the two ends connected — if upstream ever adds a `.default()` for one of these keys, it reddens and the form should declare it again.

**The arm-A select pins were re-pointed, not deleted.** Four of them used `http_request.method` as their exemplar, so this change would have left objectui#6830 arm A's select half demonstrated on a claim the contract refuses — green, and about nothing. They now stand on `end.outcome`, a declaration the spec genuinely backs, with the expected text derived from the installed spec rather than spelled out. The `http_request` rows that pin the control's existence, its option roster and its deprecated-value fallback are unchanged and still pass: this PR deleted a **declaration**, not an editor.

**Out of scope, noted and not filed.** The card's own secondary observation — `approval.maxRevisions` declaring `defaultValue: '3'` alongside a hand-written `placeholder: '3'`, where the number control reads only the placeholder — is untouched here. The card itself rules it not worth its own card, and it dissolves if the number control ever reads `defaultValue` the way the boolean and select controls do.
